title: Cue Calibration Grotto
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchbook for small, fast experiments around cue calibration — probing how small changes to exemplar order, anchor phrasing, and noise injection affect generation stability and failure modes. Not a polished report; for transfer, copy interesting sections into Confluence + link tests.

Mental model: the Grotto
- Think of a grotto as a damp, changeable chamber: seeds can sit and leach signal. I use the metaphor to remind myself that seemingly small environmental changes (context, ordering, punctuation) can cause slow drift.

Quick reproducible recipes (always include seed, temp, and deterministic RNG when logging):
- Recipe 1: Rotation sweep
  * Seed set: 6 exemplars (A..F) with same label distribution.
  * Procedure: permute order in 6! / sample 60 permutations, temperature=0.3, top_p=0.95, 5 runs each.
  * Observable: answer surface mode (majority vs long-tail).
  * Notes: rotate every run rather than random sampling to detect order effects.

- Recipe 2: Anchor injection
  * Prompt anchor: one-line instruction before exemplars that either: (i) paraphrases task goal, (ii) uses imperative, (iii) uses example-based anchor.
  * Measure: change in hallucination rate and brevity.

Session logs (high level):
- 2025-02-12: rotation sweep baseline. Outcome: exemplar order accounted for ~12% variance in two-step classification edgecases. Long exemplars earlier bias outputs toward verbosity.
- 2025-02-18: anchor injection. Short imperative anchor reduced over-explanation but increased missing-edge-case errors.
- 2025-02-24: injected token-noise (random punctuation) into middle exemplar; observed brittle parsing on models with smaller context windows.

Representative few-shot set (for reproduction):
- Prompt preamble: "You are an assistant that converts terse bug reports into a short actionable summary (1-2 sentences) and a risk label: low/med/high."
- Exemplars:
  1) "App crashes on login after update. Stack trace points to auth module." => "Login crash after update; auth module stack trace. Risk: high."
  2) "Button text overlaps on small screens, users can still tap." => "UI overlap on small screens; functionality intact. Risk: low."
  3) "Search sometimes returns empty list even though items exist; repro steps intermittent." => "Intermittent empty search results; repro unreliable. Risk: medium.

Failure cases observed (note-style):
- Anchor contradiction: when anchor uses vague phrase like "be concise" while exemplars are verbose, model oscillates between modes and sometimes outputs nothing.
- Overfitting to formatting: models copy exemplar punctuation and create unnatural punctuation-heavy summaries.
- Latent hallucination in rotated sets: when a particular exemplar sits first, it can prime a wrong label distribution for subsequent cases.

Hypotheses to test next (short list):
- H1: Prepending a single canonical label example (label + one-line rationale) stabilizes label selection across permutations.
- H2: Adding soft constraints ("always include a risk label") decreases label omission without increasing hallucinations if temperature <=0.4.
- H3: Minimal punctuation normalization of exemplars (strip trailing periods) reduces punctuation-copy artifacts.

Mini-experiments I want to run (alloc/ETA):
- Tiny grid: temperature {0.2,0.4}, top_p {0.9,0.95}, anchor style {imperative, example-anchored} — 24 runs — ETA 2 hours on small hosted test queue.
- Ablation: remove last exemplar from set to test recency effect — 12 runs.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add a quick eval harness that computes: label-consistency, brevity score (tokens), hallucination proxy (presence of out-of-vocab named entities). Link to GH PR.
- Turn interesting failed permutations into canned testcases for Optimize regressions.
- Share short findings with SEs investigating customer X (they care about consistent risk labels).

Random aside (brain dump):
- Tried mixing one counterexample (intentionally wrong exemplar) into set to see robustness — model tends to chase the counterexample when placed at position 2. Consider using that as stress test.

If you copy from this page: please preserve the date stamps for reproducibility and add the new experiment IDs when you run the grids.
